input: Build a capsule first-aid kit for road trips

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The kit's contents change significantly depending on whether it covers only basic wound care, or also includes medications, emergency tools, and condition-specific items — knowing the boundaries prevents over- or under-packing.
The number of travelers and their ages (e.g., young children, elderly passengers) directly affects quantities needed and which items to include, such as pediatric dosages or mobility aids.
The types of roads and destinations (urban highways vs. remote wilderness routes) determine how self-sufficient the kit needs to be and how far the traveler may be from professional medical help.
A budget ceiling determines whether to buy a pre-made kit and supplement it, or source every item individually — it also affects the quality and quantity of supplies.
Some people want a fully DIY-curated kit for maximum control, while others prefer a pre-assembled base kit they can customize — this shapes the entire assembly approach.

Knowing whether 'done well' means fitting inside a glove box, meeting a checklist standard (e.g., Red Cross guidelines), or being ready by a specific trip date sets the definition of a complete outcome.
Where the person plans to shop (online, pharmacy, outdoor retailer) and how soon they need it ready determines the recommended sourcing path and packing format.

gold.taskTitle: Build a capsule first-aid kit for road trips
gold.taskDescription: Assemble a compact, travel-ready first-aid kit specifically suited for road trip use.

questions.title: Which medical situations should this kit cover?
questions.description: Should the kit handle only basic wound care and minor injuries, or also include medications (pain relief, antihistamines), burn care, emergency tools like a CPR mask, or condition-specific supplies?

questions.title: How many people is this kit built for?
questions.description: Establish the number of travelers and whether any are children, elderly, or have known medical conditions — this affects quantities and which specific items to include.

questions.title: What kind of routes or destinations will you be driving?
questions.description: Will trips stick to busy highways near towns, or venture into remote areas far from hospitals? This determines how self-sufficient and comprehensive the kit needs to be.

questions.title: What is your budget for assembling this kit?
questions.description: A clear budget determines whether to buy a pre-made kit as a base, source all items individually, or opt for professional-grade supplies versus standard pharmacy options.

questions.title: Do you prefer building it from scratch or customizing a pre-made kit?
questions.description: Some people want full control by sourcing every item themselves; others prefer starting with a pre-assembled kit and adding to it. This shapes the entire build approach.

questions.title: What size or container requirement does the kit need to meet?
questions.description: Should it fit in a glove box, a door pocket, or is a larger bag stored in the trunk acceptable? This defines the physical boundaries of what can be included.

questions.title: Where do you plan to buy the supplies, and by when?
questions.description: Knowing whether you'll shop online, at a pharmacy, or an outdoor retailer — and whether there's an upcoming trip deadline — determines the best sourcing path and timeline.
